text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Trondheim soccer team Rosenborg beat AC Milan two goals to one in the final qualifying match of the European Cup Champion's League on Wednesday. "Its the most important moment in Rosenborg's history," said trainer Nils Arne Eggen. "We played an extraordinary match. It was very hard to play in a situation like that where we had to win."
- The Guatemalan government and leftist rebels signed a ceasefire agreement in Oslo on Wednesday, the first of several accords to end Latin America's longest civil war.

- Parliament arranged the first ever spontaneous question time on Wednesday, when members were able to ask the government any question. Most of the questions were put to Prime Minister Torbjoern Jagland on the establishing of different advisory councils.

- A poll by a Norwegian news service shows that analysts are still positive to the banking sector and expect a further increase in the banking index on the Oslo Bourse. Christiania og Kreditkassen ASA is mentioned as a good buy. Seven out of eight analysts recommend buying shares in Christiania.

- Wilhelm Wilhelmsen, Chairman of Saga Petroleum ASA, believes the share market will react positively to Saga's takeover of British-based Santa Fe Exploration. Wilhelmsen says the decision to buy Santa Fe was based on a strict profitability evaluation. Analysts were critical to the acquisition, arguing that it had paid too much for Santa Fe.
